- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). I have a complete picture. No need to wait further — the code is unambiguous.

r01.

**Premise correction:** There is no Redis anywhere in this repository, and the cache is not a separate/external "layer." This is the [usememos/memos](https://github.com/usememos/memos) Go codebase, and its cache is a **thread-safe in-memory cache** built into the `store` package. There is no `redis`/`ioredis` client, no connection host/port, and nothing to configure for a cache server — everything lives in-process.

**Actual mechanism:**

- The cache implementation is `store/cache/cache.go` — a `Cache` struct backed by a `sync.Map` with per-item `expiration` timestamps, a background `cleanupLoop`, and a `MaxItems` eviction policy. It is not connected to any external store.
- It is wired into the store in `store/store.go`. `Store.New` builds a single `cache.Config` and instantiates three in-memory caches (`store/store.go:38-52`):
  - `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — each created via `cache.New(cacheConfig)`.
- User entries specifically are cached in `userCache`. They're written with the plain `Set` call (e.g. `store/user.go:98,122,132,143,167`), which uses the **default TTL** rather than a custom one (`Set` → `SetWithTTL(..., c.config.DefaultTTL)`, `store/cache/cache.go:92-95`).

**TTL for user entries:** **10 minutes.** It comes from the shared `cacheConfig.DefaultTTL = 10 * time.Minute` set in `store/store.go:41` (matching `DefaultConfig()` in `store/cache/cache.go:59`). Alongside it: `CleanupInterval` = 5 minutes and `MaxItems` = 1000. There is no user-specific override — users, user settings, and instance settings all share the same 10-minute default TTL.

## Summary of Caching in `/bench/repo`

This is the **Memos** project — a Go backend with a React/TypeScript frontend (`web/`).

### 1. Redis — NONE

There is **no Redis anywhere** in this codebase. I searched for `redis`, `ioredis`, `Redis`, `REDIS` across all Go, JS/TS, JSON, YAML, and env files:
- No `redis` in `go.mod` / `go.sum`
- No `redis`/`ioredis` in `web/package.json`
- No connection config (no host/port/client setup) anywhere

There is also **no memcached**. Note: `github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/v2 v2.0.7` appears in `go.sum` but is **NOT in `go.mod`** and is not imported by any `.go` file — it is a transitive dependency only, unused by application code.

### 2. The Cache Layer — a custom in-memory cache

The real cache is a hand-rolled, thread-safe, TTL-based in-memory cache.

- **`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`** — the entire cache implementation. Backed by `sync.Map` + an `atomic.Int64` item counter, with a background `cleanupLoop` goroutine. Key pieces:
  - `Interface` with `Set`, `SetWithTTL`, `Get`, `Delete`, `Clear`, `Size`, `Close`
  - `Config{ DefaultTTL, CleanupInterval, MaxItems, OnEviction }`
  - `DefaultConfig()` (lines 57-64): `DefaultTTL: 10m`, `CleanupInterval: 5m`, `MaxItems: 1000`
  - Eviction: on `Get` if past `expiration`; periodic `cleanup()`; and `cleanupOldest()` drops ~20% of `MaxItems` when over capacity.

- **`/bench/repo/store/store.go`** (lines 23-58) — where caches are instantiated. Three separate cache instances share one config:
```go
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}
...
instanceSettingCache: cache.New(cacheConfig),
userCache:            cache.New(cacheConfig),
userSettingCache:     cache.New(cacheConfig),
```
All three are closed in `Store.Close()` (lines 72-78).

Frontend has an unrelated editor-draft cache at **`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/cacheService.ts`** — it uses `localStorage` (browser), keyed by username, with **no TTL/expiry**. Not relevant to server-side caching.

### 3. TTL applied to "user" entries

There is **no user-specific/custom TTL**. User entries fall under the shared `DefaultTTL` of **10 minutes** (`CleanupInterval` 5 minutes).

- **`/bench/repo/store/user.go`**:
  - `userCacheKey(userID int32)` (line 88) returns `strconv.Itoa` of the user ID.
  - Users are written via `s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user)` in `CreateUser`, `CreateUserIfNoUsers`, `UpdateUser`, `ListUsers`, and `GetUser` (lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167). `Set` uses the default 10m TTL — none of them call `SetWithTTL`.
  - `GetUser` (lines 148-168) reads cache only when looked up by `ID`; a cache miss falls through to `ListUsers` which repopulates.
- **`/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go`** (lines 39-41) — `deleteUserCache` removes the entry via `s.userCache.Delete`.
- User **settings** cache: `/bench/repo/store/cache.go` defines `getUserSettingCacheKey(userID, key)` → `"<id>-<key>"`; used in `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` (lines 59, 78, 86, 106, 122), again with the default 10m TTL.

Notably, `SetWithTTL` (custom per-entry TTL) exists in the cache API but is **never called** anywhere in the codebase — every caller uses the default-TTL `Set`.

**Bottom line:** No Redis, no memcached, no third-party cache library in use. Caching is a single custom in-memory TTL cache (`store/cache/cache.go`), instantiated three times in `store/store.go`, with users cached at the default **10-minute TTL** (no user-specific override).</result>
